title: Rust-Prover & Claude Opus 5.5 Formally Verify All 1,007 VeriContest Rust Programs in Lean 4
whyItMatters: Formally proves all 1,325 theorems across 1,007 Rust programs in Lean 4—jumping from a 13.95% Verus baseline to 100% at a median 3.2 minutes and $1.17 per proof.
summary: Runtime Verification and UIUC researchers built Rust-Prover, a Lean 4-backed Rust verification pipeline driven by Claude Opus 5.5, and formally verified every single problem in the 1,007-program VeriContest Rust benchmark (1,325 total theorems, up from the 13.95% prior Verus baseline). In a single automated run under 32 hours, the system proved 1,259 of 1,325 theorems at a median of 3.2 minutes and $1.17 per proof before completing the remaining specifications, while passing all 21,413 Rust test cases.
technicalHighlights: Formally verified 100% of VeriContest—all 1,325 theorems across 1,007 Rust programs—in Lean 4, up from 13.95% on the prior Verus baseline.
Proved 1,259/1,325 theorems in one automated run under 32 hours at median 3.2 min and $1.17 API cost per proof.
Verified programs simultaneously pass all 21,413 executable Rust test cases, bridging formal proofs with real systems code.
caveats: Demonstrated on competitive-programming-scale Rust benchmarks (VeriContest) rather than million-line OS kernels; paper is an October 2026 preprint.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates economically viable ($1.17/proof) autonomous end-to-end formal verification of imperative Rust software in Lean 4.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly accelerates industrial adoption of AI-driven formal verification for memory-safe critical systems.
scoreRationale.verification: All 1,325 theorems are kernel-checked in Lean 4 and validated against 21,413 executable Rust tests.
scoreRationale.velocity: Shattered the 13.95% baseline to 100% coverage in under 32 hours for the bulk automated pass.

sources.label: Serbanuta et al. — Solving VeriContest with a Lean-Backed Rust Verifier (arXiv:2610.03994)
